Great game. However, PC versions require fixes, but the real issue is inconsistency. It’s not a case of installing one recommended mod and being done. Solutions vary per system, and what works for some players may not work for others, often leading to time-consuming trial and error. I would've loved to play this again as it is one of my best childhood Star Wars games.
You have to mod the game in order to make it work on a modern PC. Until that is fixed it's ridiculous to take money for it.

This is one of those games that's awkward to discuss because, while the game itself is pretty good in my opinion, the port to PC did not go very well.

While arguably this, actually is not the worst Xbox > PC port, it's still not a great one. You need to follow a multi-step guide to figure out how to get this game to co-operate with modern resolutions and in widescreen. This process involves multiple mods that all need to be installed in their correct order, you have to patch an 'editable' version of the game's .exe which you also have to download, and on top of all that, the game needs to be capped to like 60fps or thereabouts to prevent a certain bug from preventing you from moving after combat ends.

This is all a massive pain, to say the least.

However, there are things that I think aged quite well. This is a pretty good looking game, for late 2003. Most of the textures and such, actually seem pretty high resolution, or at least seem pretty sharp and pleasant to look at. It's kind of stunning, given there are games released even on the 360 that are actually more ugly than this game.

Granted, this does not completely extend to people. The environment is pretty, but characters are obviously not incredible to look at. That's okay with me though. It helps that a lot of the characters you're interacting with are either aliens, or robots, or something else. There's Humans and such too of course, but having weird looking dudes helps make it not stand out as much that they are quite low fidelity.

I also was considering replaying the game to get a fresh take on the story, but I have completed this game at least 8 times or something in the past, so you know what, I'm just gonna go off memory. I played this game like a LOT on the original Xbox.

The game suffers pretty strongly from many of the pitfalls of early alignment systems. Sort of. I mean, I dunno. People for years have kinda been down on games like this for having the division between, a good choice and a bad c…
you have to install like 4 'fixes' that dont even work to try making it playable on a monitor made after 2005

Great game. One of the best rpgs ive ever played years ago. Cant play on a widescreen monitor without jumping through a bunch of hoops, with no guarantee any of the fixes will work. I just cant play this, with the experience smashed vertically or the game played in a small window.
This may be an unpopular opinion.. but if I have to got through 6 websites to mod the game for it to work on modern systems... I cannot recommend for average user.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as outdated, slow, and clunky.

citations.review_text:
Knights of the Old Republic is Dungeons & Dragons wearing Jedi robes.

Lightsabers clash, blasters fire, and invisible dice quietly decide whether anyone actually hit. The controls are ancient, Taris takes its time, and the inventory feels like legislation passed by the Galactic Senate.

Then the companions start talking.

A Jedi questions your choices. A soldier questions your motives. A homicidal protocol droid calls everyone “meatbags” and somehow becomes the most reasonable person on the ship.

The combat aged.

The story still understands Star Wars better than most of what came after it.

I don't see why this is rated as one of the best RPG games.
I'm sure that the story is good but good lord, the gameplay loop is probably the worst ♥♥♥♥ I've seen in any game ever.

Start a quest, see an enemy, tap which attack you want to do, watch your character desperately swing their weapon for a bit until the enemy is dead, repeat.

If I wanted to play a clicker game I would've played Cookie Clicker. Not Star Wars.
If you want to play an actually good RPG, go play Final Fantasy or Fallout, not this slop.
i played this on the og xbox alot. game is sick and a great story. gameplay is super outdated tho. I liked it. play it.
only worth playing if you don't care about combat feeling horrible

STAR WARS Knights of the Old Republic is a classic that fully deserves its reputation. I had already finished the game before (not on Steam). The narrative, characters, and choices are excellent and easily one of the best stories in the Star Wars universe.
The gameplay is still good and functional, but it is clearly very outdated. Combat and mechanics can feel slow and clunky, especially for new players.
Overall, I totally recommend this game to anyone who loves the Star Wars saga and enjoys classic RPGs. Despite its age, the story alone makes it worth playing.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that controller support is either terrible or absent, forcing reliance on mouse and keyboard.

citations.review_text:
KOTOR 1 and 2 are some of my favorite games of all time. I beat both several times over on my og xbox as a kid and they're a main reason I'm as big of a Star Wars fan as I am today. But if there was ever a title in need of a remaster, it's KOTOR 1. Maybe it's rose colored glasses but I don't remember ever having so many issues on the xbox. Constant crashing, graphical glitches, and the bugs; good lord almighty, THE BUGS. Mission bugs, item bugs, sound bugs, randomly being unable to move after exiting combat and needing to reload a save, the resolution shrinking during space travel and terrible controller support. Normally I'd address issues with mods but this game is old and the tools provided by the modding community are outdated or broken/unintuitve. 

Despite that, the core is still as beautiful as ever. The story is the why; some of the dialogue and choices are a bit ham fisted but there honestly hasn't been another rpg that allows you to be a jedi in the star wars universe. You can be a beacon for others to follow, or an absolute sicko who does what he wants when he wants. I've missed these characters (HK-47 is still the best droid) very much and if you've never played it before and are a fan of the genre, I'd strongly suggest it for the plot alone. Just be prepared, the edges are ROUGH.

This game is super glitchy. Sometimes when the characters speak a different language it doesn't show the subtitles and you can't understand what they are saying. Also, when you get stuck on a corner the keys to back up and move forward don't work and I always have to save and load to get moving forward again. Also, sometimes for no reason I am not able to move. It is not compatible with an Xbox controller even though this was originally a game played on the original Xbox. I didn't like the tutorials because they were hard to understand and they didn't explain the game clearly enough. I played this game because my hubby is a huge star wars fan and wanted me to play it with him. The mechanics are similar to D&D 4th Edition.

An oldie but a goodie.

Unfortunately the lack of support for gamepad makes it extremely difficult to get past the space battle scenes. It will forever just remain a fond memory. 

Sadly, I have to give it a thumbs down on modern hardware.

(Yes I tried all the Steam input configuration overrides for gamepads.)

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game requires troubleshooting, community patches, or modding to function and display properly on modern widescreen hardware.

citations.review_text: Its amazing, but you need mods to fix wide screen and the graphics to play it these days

KOTOR is a good game. It has good story, it has good build setups. Maybe so-so combat, but still passable.

It's just that modern systems are not built for KOTOR, KOTOR is not built for modern systems. If you have never ever modded before, do not start with modding KOTOR to work for you. Maybe start with installing mods for a more established game, like Minecraft. Get familiar with navigating caveats. Mod tools are good, you just have to use your brain to figure out the vague idea of what you are doing in any given modding guide.

Modding it into workable shape isn't too hard, but it took me 7 minutes to find the right guide, 30 or so minutes to install everything right, and then 2 and a half hours to figure out what process was incorrectly elaborated in the original guide and what I needed to do to fix it (I needed to do stuff with letterboxes, but running the program where I said no before to say yes later did not work, had to do fresh install).

If you wanted the game to just be functional, I suppose it might take 15 minutes at most in the exact processes, but set aside an hour to deal with unique problems you will have to deal with on your end that you will have to resolve on your own.

Still, I liked this game and had fun, so I can't say it's bad. 

Oh, also make sure to save every minute, have 3 saves you save periodically between, and have extra backup saves on top of that. This game crashes about every hour, and when you save can occasionally corrupt the file you save on. Isn't that scary :P
What a pain in the anus to get widescreen and hud working properly, but worth it.  If you’re ready to mess with that, it's still good.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe a game-breaking bug where characters freeze or are unable to move after combat encounters, which can be mitigated by capping the framerate to 60fps or through save-and-reload workarounds.

citations.review_text:
Really fun, I like the choices. Only major complaints are some weird visual bugs on Dantooine I needed to go into my graphics settings to fix, and an odd one where playable characters will sometimes get stuck and unable to move after combat if they animation cancelled halfway through attacking. Sometimes the whole party could get stuck. I just saved and reloaded, but it happens a lot, so just be aware.

Besides that, the story is really fun, and I like the dynamics. Combat is fun, and there's a lot of fun character builds.

Can't go wrong with this classic. Although on modern systems you have to cap the frame rate to 60fps and turn on v-sync otherwise you'll run into a game breaking bug where you can't move after a combat encounter. Hopefully the Remake will live up to the original whenever that releases.

I have really enjoyed playing this game. I bought it on my phone, played multiple playthroughs, learned there were mods, and bought the game on PC. I had to cap my framerate to 60 (googled how to do it) to stop whichever character I was controlling from being unable to move after combat, but it ran smoothly after I fixed it. I only crashed once when entering a glitchy area in the sleheyron mod, and am now starting brotherhood of shadow mod playthrough. 10/10 would recommend.

This game is a buggy mess, and I really want to like it, but it's so hard when there's so much in the way of enjoying the game. I've played this with the community patch, no other mods.

In the Undercity in Taris, the grass was causing the game to crash. Turning off the grass and I could continue.

Then not much later, the game kept crashing again. Turning on Windows XP SP3 compatibility mode allowed me to continue.

In the ruins on Dantooine a certain cutscene didn't trigger. Luckily I had a save I could revert to.

That's just the gamebreaking bugs. There are so many other ones, like not being able to move after combat (have to save and reload, permanent solution was not using v-sync to cap the framerate, but rivatuner), characters not responding (save and reload), getting stuck by running into my party members, party members being on the other end of the map when you want to transition to the next and having to wait for them to walk your way etc. etc.

If you're willing to deal with all of that, you'll find an early version of Mass Effect, but it's Star Wars. I was surprised the game has a few unexpected twists and turns in the story, and they really allow you to go evil/sith if you want to.

1 playthrough on normal, light side.

claims.claim: Players describe the vanilla PC version as lacking native widescreen resolution support and having interface controls that feel clunky.

citations.review_text: The game is well-written and still holds up. My biggest issue has to do with the resolution settings, each resolution is stuck in a 4:3 aspect ratio, and isn't positioned on the center of the screen. There was only one setting that allowed me to center the game, although I forget exactly what it is.

Just finished my first playthrough in nearly a quarter century, and the game still holds up. A solid RPG experience, from the time when everyone was excited for the next Star Wars anything, and BioWare was an exciting new company. 

The game is similar to later BioWare games like Mass Effect, where you've got several main planet-quests you can travel between, companion characters that fight alongside you, and conversational chains that follow overall choices you make. A pleasant way to blow 30-40 hours, with some replay value if you want to try for different endings.

There are a couple major issues, however: 

- This was originally an OG Xbox game, and the PC port didn't do a good job with controls. The mouse and keyboard interface is very clunky. It takes time to get used to, and even when you do, it's still bad. It can make some of the movement-based puzzles infuriating. Unfortunately the PC version *doesn't* support game controllers, so you're stuck with the keyboard/mouse. I can't imagine it would be any fun on a steam deck.

- The vanilla game has some problems on modern Windows, especially with full-screen mode and supporting wide-screen (non-4:3) resolutions. You may need to make some edits in the ini files and replace some game files to get it to work smoothly. Fortunately a quick Google search should give you simple instructions on making any fixes.

- The vanilla game also looks it's age, with the primitive models and low-res textures capable of running on an OG Xbox. You can significantly improve your experience if you install some of the fan-created graphic upgrade mods and bug fixes. There's no Steam workshop support, so you've got to do it the old fashioned way. I used the "Full Kotor Overall" mod collection over on Nexus.

All these caveats aside, it's still a game I'd recommend if you like this kind of RPG, or Star Wars in general. And the price is right, especially if you find it on sale.

Albeit straightforward, it's safe to say it doesn't come in the way of the most important part of KOTOR: The journey - I chose the dark side and was pleasantly rewarded with some cool set pieces, however the ending felt rushed and shortlived. Nonetheless enjoyed my time and looking forward to playing the second game one day. 

Also I see the appeal in HK47, what a droid lmao.

One of the best plot twists in fiction, amazing characters and a fun retro styling to it. If you can get past the somewhat clunky controls and dated (though imo charming) graphics then you'll have a great time.

If you simply look past its hundreds of bugs this game is phenomenal. Sure the graphics are terrible and the combat is clunky, but the story is great so it's fine. 10/10 very nostalgic and the sort of fun that is addicting.

Holds up surprisingly well. The story is great, and I had fun with character specialization and itemization. Worst aspect was the combat, which felt a bit janky and frustrating at worst and a little boring/repetitive at best.
Some of its mechanics are a bit clunky by modern day standards but it still holds up very well and is a very fun game. I'm not surprised it's considered by many to be one of the best Star Wars games.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that running the game on modern hardware requires technical workarounds, community fixes, or windowed mode to prevent crashing or display issues.

citations.review_text: KOTOR has an outstanding story, cast of characters, soundtrack, and art design, even rivaling the standards of the Star Wars films. The gameplay hasn't aged well in some respects, as certain mechanics are far too powerful or pointless. And be warned, unless you run it in a window, it will break. Badly. A shame this beautiful tale is held back by the age of its scripting.

This is an all time great game and it’s incredible to think something with this much depth came out in 2003. Yes, the combat is a little clunky but the rest of the game makes up for it. One important note though, and I cannot stress this enough… do not, I repeat, DO NOT play this game on Steam Deck. It is just straight up broken. It crashes often, it has major graphical bugs, sometimes you can’t even make it past the main menu, sometimes you literally can’t get through a cutscene without crashing. I had to use every tool at my disposal to make this game crawl across the finish line. Changing every kind of menu option available, applying new launch commands, finding community made protons for comparability, making changes to the key commands in the games .ini file, installing patches, uninstalling and reinstalling. I only made it through because I’m moronically stubborn. Do NOT make my mistake. If you’re thinking of buying this to play on Steam Deck, don’t do it.

This is the 2nd RPG game I have played, 1st one being KOTOR 2 lol, completely ducked up the order.

Story -> We begin our journey as a mere soldier for the Republic then takes our path as a Padawan once we realize that we can feel the Force & just when we make ourselves stronger we encounter the main villian of the game, who then literally drops the biggest bombshell of a surprise on us.

Gameplay -> Turn based combat but it's really fun once you get used to it, we have different classes to choose from, different feats, powers & we can even customize some of our weapons & armors.

Graphics -> For a game that came out in 2003, this must have been groundbreaking but to me it's kinda surprising that we can't run this game on full screen, I tried but nothing worked although the textures are great.

Conclusion -> KOTOR Remake is in development currently but I don't know when it will be out plus I had to do some tweaks just to launch this game on Windows 10 but it was completely worth it, the game has no bugs & if you don't want to wait for the Remake or want the OG experience then it's totally worth it, hands down this is the best Star Wars game of all time.

I absolutely recommend this game WITH A CAVEAT: be prepared to jump through some HOOPS (installing mods) to get the game running at widescreen resolution. There's apparently a Switch version and (I think?) a mobile version, plus there are *emus* (the bird, definitely the bird ;D ) that I'd guess can reliably run the old console version(s). Look into your options before buying this one. I just happened to already have this on Steam from a LONG time ago (in a galaxy blah blah blah...) so of course I was determined to make it work on a PC from 20 years in the future.

FOR CONTENT CREATORS: if you have any intention of recording or streaming the game, bear in mind 2 things before buying this version:
1. the cutscenes don't capture natively, not with game or display capture. You'll need a capture card to stream them or have to rip them from somewhere to cut into a video.
2. Even with all the work required to get the game running native on a widescreen monitor, it will NOT run in fullscreen borderless (I couldn't find anything that would work anyway, and I spent HOURS one day fixing and tweaking and modding things). This wouldn't be the end of the world, except if you alt-tab out or alt-enter or ctrl-alt-del or whatever, the game will minimize and not reopen, effectively crashing. This also makes streaming or recording or any kind of multitasking a massive pain with only one PC. The only solution I could come up with was to move all my streaming software, settings, and peripherals over to my second PC and stream from there. Alternately, you can just run the game in windowed mode, but I personally would rather put my [redacted] in a vise.

Instead of a remake, just make this game run on modern systems.

Do like you did with 'KOTOR II,' where you add some modern features. Modern resolutions, steam achievements, steam workshop.

Why not? It'd be pure pazaak.

I only got into Star Wars about 2 years ago, but since then I have worked through all of the content within the entire canon timeline (Video games, movies, shows, except I have yet to read all of the comics, I've only read a few series).

So, now I've moved onto the EU and older, non-canon content such as this and, man.. I understand what all of the hype is about now!

Admittedly, my expectations were low because I usually only play AAA games with stellar graphics and whatnot, and I appreciate great visuals. I also was not too enthused about being unable to play with a controller. (I know, I know..)

I was only let down further when I discovered the bug where you have to save and load constantly in order to regain control of your character.. not to mention the random crashes, of course..

But in spite of all of that, I absolutely loved this game. It has a great story, the lore is expansive, and combat is actually quite satisfying once you get used to it.. just be sure to constantly save!

The story branching is impressive. I constantly found myself in disbelief that so much love had been put into this game way back in the day. I feel it's something that is missing in modern games. Most "choices" in games are illusionary and inconsequential. Pretty sad.

Anyway, I recommend grabbing some mods and firing it up if you love Star Wars. I mean, I completed it *just earlier today* and am already thinking about how I'll run my next playthrough, which will be in a few years so it feels fresh.

10/10, hands down.
